setlist.title: It's All Over Now, Baby Blue

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Standing On The Moon** (3 reviews): Post-drums run of Standing on the Moon into Miracle into Morning Dew singled out as outstanding; Three of the four songs after space are Jerry tunes, making a great backstretch [18][25][26]
- **Samson & Delilah** (1 review): Early second set, from Samson through Drums, rated incredible [21]
- **Iko Iko** (1 review): Iko Iko was ripping [21]
- **It's All Over Now, Baby Blue** (1 review): Reviewer calls it the best post-drums segment of the nineties [18]
- **Phil & Keyboards Jam** (1 review): The Phil and keyboards jam coming out of He's Gone was called simply beautiful [16]
- **No MSG Jam** (1 review): The jam Dick's Picks calls the No MSG Jam is described as a monster [20]

## Setlist highlights

- **Miracle**: rare: 13 archived performances [28]

## The recordings

- **gd90-09-16.schoeps-fob.sacks.9435.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): source not stated; 21 songs; 193 min; rated 4.38/5 by 21 [1]. Said about its sound: Recording is pretty good; Post-drums section is great and the recording is good; Audience tape has a warmth that soundboards sometimes lack, bringing back the feeling of being there [21][22][24][25][26]
- **gd1990-09-16.schoeps.wiley.11663.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 183 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [3]. Said about its sound: A digital pop in He's Gone on the left channel was replaced using the right channel [3]
- **gd1990-09-16.aud.andrewf.92158.flac16**: audience recording; 21 songs; 183 min [4]
- **gd1990-09-16.145946.mtx.seamons.ht115.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 187 min [6]. Said about its sound: Two loud, distracting bursts of sound were reduced, one in each set [6]

## Around the show

- Hornsby adds a 1970s touch, and Vince, new at the time, played his best [24]
- A man in the upper deck on Jerry's side jumped a railing, fell 15-20 feet, then walked away [27]
- Most of the jam in He's Gone was played by Phil, Bruce and Vince only [3]
- Followed a weak show on the 15th; the band delivered the performance fans had been waiting for with Welnick [16]
- Second set was hot and set the band up for a magical run afterward [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd90-09-16.schoeps-fob.sacks.9435.sbeok.shnf**: source: MAD> D> CD>WAV>SHN [1]. Also: Soundboards were pulled, so the audience recordings are the ones available; This show was released as Dick's Picks 9; Transfer chain went from MAD to D to CD [1][24][26]
- **gd1990-09-16.schoeps.wiley.11663.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Dave Brotman; transferred by Tim Wiley; source: FOB-AUD(Schoeps)>DAT>CDR> [3]. Also: T. Wiley converted, edited and seeded it in August 2002, using source disks from Paul B [3]
- **gd1990-09-16.aud.andrewf.92158.flac16**: taped by Andrew F; transferred by Andrew F; source: OTS AUD: Nakamichi CM300's w/CP4 shotguns > patched thru one Sony TC-D5M > [4]. Also: Patches from ShnID-11663 cover tape flips in the Phil jam and the start of Morning Dew [4]
- **gd1990-09-16.145946.mtx.seamons.ht115.flac16**: source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons [6]. Also: This date appears on Dick's Picks 9 [6]
